 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Shockwaves continue to be felt across the boxing world following the withdrawal of Jai Opetaia from his match against Deontay Wilder. This was the chief support for Fury vs AJ, and its removal has left the undercard looking terrible.
 Some fans are talking about skipping the undercard altogether and just turning up drunk for the main event at 1am.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement But efforts are underway to find a replacement. Derek Chisora has said he's happy to step in for a rematch of his fight with Deontay last year. While Derek is always entertaining, he was a clear loser last time, and it was only Wilder's compassion that spared him from being knocked out. Chisora is also about to turn 43 and is being urged by the many fans who care about him to retire.
 the British heavyweight champion, Richard Riakporhe is also in the frame as a replacement. The "Midnight Train" is a big-punching former cruiserweight who could certainly be a problem for the ageing Wilder.
 And now we have Jarrell "Big Baby" Miller coming forward. He is likely to appeal to Netflix, who want to boost the appeal of the event for US audiences. Miller would lay on some fun trash-talking during the build-up, and his relentless, come-forward style should blend well with Wilder's sharpshooting approach.
 Who will actually step in will come down to money of course, and both Chisora and Miller will be asking for a lot of it to come in at short notice. That leads us to speculate on what caused Opetaia to pull out in the first place.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The official story cites the cause as a hand injury that was sustained in his last fight against Norair Mikaeljan, and made worse during training. But boxing insider, Dan Rafael, who broke the news about Opetaia, says none of his sources mentioned injury as a reason for the pull-out.
 Rafael also said that Opetaia's team had lobbied the WBC at their recent convention to have Jai installed as the mandatory challenger for the cruiserweight title. Why would they do that when Opetaia was about to move up to heavyweight?
 Could it be that there is more money up for grabs in a cruiserweight unification fight with David Benavidez than there is for fighting the likes of Wilder up at heavyweight?
 Not long ago, it was assumed that if the Saudis were involved, the money would be generous, but it seems that things are changing. Saudi Arabia has had to rethink its investment in sport, now their country is caught up in a war that is escalating.
 If money has caused the chief support match to fall through, how safe is the main event between Fury and AJ?
